CveFindings.Description:
[CVE-2015-3253](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qg25-hgjv-cg9q): Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component in Apache Groovy

Severity: CRITICAL

Affected dependencies:
- org.codehaus.groovy:groovy-all:2.1.2 (declared at build.gradle:8); affected range: >= 1.7.0, <= 2.4.3; first patched version: 2.4.4.

Recommended fix: Upgrade to a supported release outside all affected ranges; the advisory's first patched version is a minimum fix for that advisory, not a complete upgrade recommendation. Guava uses Android/JRE release variants; select the applicable patched variant.

Applicability: dependency-version match only, not proof of reachable exploitation. Dependency CLI failed (Gradle 1.4 HTTP download returned 403); only five directly declared dependencies, including test dependencies, were queried. Transitive dependencies were not resolved.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Initialization
CweFindings.Description: The product does not initialize or incorrectly initializes a resource, which might leave the resource in an unexpected state when it is accessed or used.
CweFindings.Explanation: VendingMachine.reportingURL defaults to null; sendTransactionReport dereferences it at line 117 without requiring or checking setReportingURL initialization. Calling reporting before configuration fails in the submitted task. This is a potential code-quality pattern, not demonstrated attacker exploitation.

CweFindings.Name: Incorrect Calculation
CweFindings.Description: The product performs a calculation that generates incorrect or unintended results that are later used in security-critical decisions or resource management.
CweFindings.Explanation: VendingMachine.removeLargestCoinFromChange performs change.remove(biggestSmallerCoin) inside assert. With assertions disabled, returned coins remain in recorded inventory and later refunds can select already-returned coins, causing incorrect resource accounting.

CweFindings.Name: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime
CweFindings.Description: The product does not release a resource after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the resource is no longer needed.
CweFindings.Explanation: Each VendingMachine creates a single-thread executor. Once reporting starts its worker, task completion does not release the executor/thread; no shutdown lifecycle exists.

CweFindings.Name: Missing Release of File Descriptor or Handle after Effective Lifetime
CweFindings.Description: The product does not release a file descriptor or handle after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the file descriptor/handle is no longer needed.
CweFindings.Explanation: VendingMachine.sendTransactionReport obtains the HTTP response input stream and discards it without closing it; no enclosing cleanup releases the response handle.

CweFindings.Name: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
CweFindings.Description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.
CweFindings.Explanation: VendingMachine.transactionLog is an ArrayDeque shared by caller-thread purchase() additions (line 54) and the internal reporting executor (lines 106, 113-121), which reads/removes entries without synchronization. Serializing reporting tasks does not serialize purchases with the worker. CWE-567, CWE-662 and CWE-820 describe this same underlying queue race, not three independent defects. Static pattern confirmed; no runtime reproduction or remote exploitability demonstrated.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Synchronization
CweFindings.Description: The product utilizes multiple threads or processes to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.
CweFindings.Explanation: VendingMachine.transactionLog is an ArrayDeque shared by caller-thread purchase() additions (line 54) and the internal reporting executor (lines 106, 113-121), which reads/removes entries without synchronization. Serializing reporting tasks does not serialize purchases with the worker. CWE-567, CWE-662 and CWE-820 describe this same underlying queue race, not three independent defects. Static pattern confirmed; no runtime reproduction or remote exploitability demonstrated.

CweFindings.Name: Missing Synchronization
CweFindings.Description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.
CweFindings.Explanation: VendingMachine.transactionLog is an ArrayDeque shared by caller-thread purchase() additions (line 54) and the internal reporting executor (lines 106, 113-121), which reads/removes entries without synchronization. Serializing reporting tasks does not serialize purchases with the worker. CWE-567, CWE-662 and CWE-820 describe this same underlying queue race, not three independent defects. Static pattern confirmed; no runtime reproduction or remote exploitability demonstrated.

CweFindings.Name: Insufficient Logging
CweFindings.Description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.
CweFindings.Explanation: VendingMachine.returnCoins (lines 81-90) deducts monetary credit and requests physical coin refunds without recording amounts, outcomes, or partial-refund failures. This is a potential transaction-reconciliation audit gap; purchase auditing exists separately at line 54. No remote exploitability is established.

Limitations: Security-only assessment. Core Java cloud-readiness and Java-upgrade assessment was not run: neither appmod-run-assessment-action nor appmod-precheck-assessment MCP tool is available. Configure the Java assessment MCP server to expose either tool, then rerun the assessment skill. Empty core rules/incidents mean NOT ASSESSED, not zero migration issues.

Six raw CVE matches; only two critical matches retained at minimum severity high. Version matches do not establish reachable exploitation.

Static CWE review of eight production Java files; tests, generated code, dependency internals, external callers, hardware implementations and deployment integrations excluded. No runtime verification. NOT_FOUND means no pattern observed within this scope, not proof of safety.
Eight CWE matches represent six underlying concerns: CWE-567, CWE-662 and CWE-820 overlap on one shared-queue race. CWE severity potential is an assessment classification, not CVSS severity.
